did.unittitle: Shore Road and Bay Ridge photographs
did.abstract: Set of 40 black and white photographs from an album depicting places in Bay Ridge, including Shore Road, P.S. 102, Ridge Boulevard, and Colonial Road.

altformavail.head: Existence and Location of Copies
altformavail.p: The digitized portions of this collection are available on our digital collections under the call number prefix SHORE.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The photographs are housed in one folder and the album pages from which they have been separated in another.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: Bay Ridge is a neighborhood in southwestern Brooklyn. The area was originally called Yellow Hook after the color of its soil. After the yellow fever epidemic of 1848-1849, the area was renamed Bay Ridge in 1853 to avoid association with the disease. In the later 19th century, the area became a wealthy enclave with mansions lining the high ridge of the nieghborhood's name and overlooking the harbor. The subway came to the area in 1915, and large apartment buildings were increasingly built around it. The photographs in this collection depict the era before the neighborhood was developed and the subway brought lower-income and immigrant populations to the area.

list.head: Source:
list.item: Rawson, Elizabeth Reich. "Bay Ridge." In The Encyclopedia of New York City, edited by Kenneth T. Jackson, 104-105. New Haven, Conn.: Yale University Press; New York: New-York Historical Society, 2010.

phystech.head: Physical Characteristics and Technical Requirements
phystech.p: The collection's digital surrogates should be used in place of the originals whenever possible.

prefercite.p: Identification of item, date (if known); Shore Road and Bay Ridge photographs, BCMS.0102, Object ID number; Brooklyn Public Library, Center for Brooklyn History.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The photographs were digitized and described on the item level at some point following their acquisition in 2001. The collection was rehoused and this finding created by Dee Bowers in 2026.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: Bay Ridge photographs in the Brooklyn photograph and illustration collection (ARC.202) and Brooklyn Daily Eagle photographs (BCMS.0002)
Bay Ridge postcards in the Brooklyn postcards collection (BCMS.0060) and the Joan Kay postcard collection (BCMS.0094)
Bay Ridge ephemera in the Brooklyn ephemera collection (BCMS.0007) and the Brooklyn Historical Society ephemera collection (ARC.272)
Crescent Athletic Club collection (ARC.178) and Crescent Athletic Club photograph albums (ARC.236)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Set of 40 black and white photographs from an album depicting places along Shore Road and elsewhere in Bay Ridge. Subjects include P.S. 102, the canon at Fort Hamilton (now John Paul Jones Park), the Crescent Athletic Club and its boat house, Dutch Reformed Church, old Christ Church, Church of Our Lady of Angels, the Perry Estate, Ridge Boulevard, the Dowling House, Colonial Road, and views of the bay and harbor, including one image of crowds watching the 1909 Hudson-Fulton celebration.

The album has been disassembled and the photographs removed from the deteriorating black paper pages. The original pages with their handwritten captions have been retained in their own folder, but the captions have also been transcribed on the versos of the photographic prints.
